groups.title: Tablet (104303ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the treatment of infection with roundworm, pinworm, hookworm (Ancylostoma), whipworm, American hookworm (Necator) and threadworm (Strongyloides), and of mixed infections with these worms.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 24 months and older: for pinworm, take 1 tablet (400 mg), 1 time in 1 day. To eradicate the infection, take 1 further tablet (400 mg) once more 7 days later. For roundworm, hookworm, whipworm and American hookworm, take 1 tablet (400 mg) as a single dose. For severe mixed infection of threadworm with another parasite (tapeworm), take 1 tablet (400 mg), 1 time in 1 day, for 3 days. If it is hard to swallow, the tablet may be chewed or taken with a small amount of water; no special measures such as stopping meals or using a laxative are needed. An examination is carried out 3 weeks after treatment, and if the infection has not been cured a second course may be given in some cases.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver impairment or kidney impairment, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5. Before taking this medicine, always make sure that you are not pregnant. It may affect clinical test values: occasionally a reversible fall in the white blood cell count and a mild to moderate rise in liver enzyme values may occur.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with theophylline, cimetidine, praziquantel, dexamethasone, ritonavir, phenytoin, carbamazepine or phenobarbital.

If Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), erythema multiforme, gastrointestinal disturbance such as nausea, vomiting, heartburn, diarrhoea, upper abdominal or abdominal pain, headache or dizziness, or, rarely, hypersensitivity reactions such as fever, generalised reddening of the skin, rash, itching or urticaria, or reversible hair loss occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Treatment of roundworm, pinworm, hookworm, whipworm, American hookworm and threadworm infection and mixed infections

groups.title: Tablet (142301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not exceed 4 tablets (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious cardiovascular adverse reactions may occur.

Taking this medicine may cause serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as bleeding, ulceration and perforation of the gastrointestinal tract.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation during treatment with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure, high blood pressure, or a history of hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you are in early or mid pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have had major surgery with blood loss; if you are being given a diuretic or an ACE inhibitor; or if you have a blood clotting disorder or are being given an anticoagulant.

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (for example a potassium-sparing diuretic, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, an immunosuppressant such as ciclosporin or tacrolimus, trimethoprim or heparin), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, or low-dose aspirin.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely triggering of an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; rarely jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbance such as scotoma or dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; rarely mental disturbance, agitation, excitement, disorientation or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral oedema, acute pulmonary oedema, fluid retention, high blood pressure or heart failure; Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency; reduced fertility in women; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.

groups.title: Oral Solution (A49300ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment of liver disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 10 to 30 mL in 1 day, divided into doses taken between meals. Dilute 10 mL of this medicine in about half a cup of water and take it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have kidney disease, or if you have or have had myocardial infarction.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had hypersensitivity to caramel.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine by mouth only; do not use it for injection. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (172806ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, back pain, dysmenorrhoea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults: take 1/2 tablet to 1.5 tablets (200 to 600 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day; up to 3200 mg may be taken in 1 day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis: take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight in 1 day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults: take 1/2 tablet to 1 tablet (200 to 400 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not take more than the recommended dose. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy; if you are taking high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have liver cirrhosis, or liver impairment now or in the past; if you have kidney impairment now or in the past; if you have cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, low-dose aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an ACE inhibitor, lithium, furosemide or a thiazide diuretic, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like) or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

If an increased risk of myocardial infarction or stroke, or serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration or perforation occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: signs of shock (heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure); blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit, reduced haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as raised GOT, GPT or ALP, liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbance such as blind spots, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); raised blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; swelling around the eyes, swelling of the face, malaise, fever, nosebleed or peripheral oedema.

groups.title: Tablet (A13500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for contraception and for the treatment of moderate acne in women who can take this medicine.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet a day for 21 days in the order marked on the pack, then have 7 days without tablets. It is best to take it at about the same time every day. Menstruation occurs during the 7 days without tablets and usually starts 2 to 3 days after the last tablet. If you continue with this medicine, start a new pack of tablets after the 7 days without tablets; menstruation may not have finished before the new pack is started. Refer to the detailed approved product information for further details.
groups.caution:
Because the risk of serious cardiovascular events such as thrombosis may be increased, women taking an oral contraceptive should refrain from smoking. Smokers aged 35 years and older must not take this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; a tumour (for example breast cancer, endometrial cancer, pituitary tumour); thrombophlebitis, thromboembolism, cerebrovascular or coronary artery disease; undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding; severe high blood pressure; severe liver impairment; Dubin-Johnson syndrome; Rotor syndrome; jaundice; cholestasis; hepatitis; sickle cell anaemia; severe diabetes; high blood lipids; hyperlipoproteinaemia; porphyria; a metabolic disorder; persistent itching during pregnancy; herpes gestationis; pemphigoid gestationis; otosclerosis; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a pituitary tumour, galactorrhoea or high blood prolactin; if you have migraine with warning signs such as scotoma or fortification spectra; if you have valvular heart disease complicated by pulmonary hypertension or atrial fibrillation; pancreatitis; valvular heart disease with a history of subacute bacterial endocarditis; diabetes with vascular lesions; headache with focal neurological symptoms such as an aura; if you are taking a direct-acting antiviral for hepatitis C; if you have a congenital or acquired hypercoagulable disorder; if you are a smoker aged 35 years and older; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are a smoker; if you have high blood pressure or obesity; if you are a woman aged 40 years and older; if you have epilepsy or migraine; if you have had arterial disease or varicose veins; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus; if you have had breast cancer; if you have or have had depression; if you have heart or kidney failure; if you have atypical hyperplastic breast disease; if you have had breast nodules; if you have valvular heart disease or atrial fibrillation; if you have had high blood lipids; if you have had gallbladder disease or gallstones; if you have endometriosis; if you have asthma or melasma; if you have peripheral circulatory disturbance; if you have diabetes; or if you have migraine without aura.

This medicine does not protect against HIV infection (AIDS) or other sexually transmitted diseases. If you have a severe gastrointestinal disease, absorption may be incomplete, so use an additional method of contraception. This medicine is not for women before their first menstruation or after the menopause. Check the detailed approved product information for full precautions.

Do not take it together with a direct-acting antiviral for hepatitis C (combinations such as ombitasvir, paritaprevir and ritonavir), phenytoin, barbiturates, primidone, carbamazepine, rifampicin, rufinamide, aprepitant, bosentan, efavirenz, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, felbamate, griseofulvin, St John's wort, lipid-lowering medicines or antibiotics. Do not take it with grapefruit juice.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: cardiovascular events (thrombophlebitis, thrombosis and arterial thromboembolism, stroke, cerebral haemorrhage, cerebral thrombosis, myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, raised blood pressure, worsening of varicose veins); urogenital symptoms (bleeding between periods, changes in menstrual volume, absence of menstruation and the like); breast symptoms (breast tenderness and enlargement, galactorrhoea, breast pain and the like); digestive symptoms (nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, liver impairment and the like); central nervous system symptoms (headache, migraine, depression, dizziness and the like); skin symptoms (melasma, acne, erythema multiforme and the like); eye symptoms (visual disturbance, change in corneal refraction and the like); hearing disturbance; metabolic symptoms (sodium and fluid retention and the like); weight change, appetite change, change in libido, speech disturbance, or hypersensitivity reactions (urticaria, angioedema and the like). Check the detailed approved product information for full adverse reactions.

groups.title: Tablet (157301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn and acid eructation (sour belching).
groups.usage: Those aged 16 years and older: take 1 tablet (10 mg) per dose; up to 2 tablets (20 mg) may be taken in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to H2 receptor antagonists, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have difficulty swallowing food or pain when swallowing, or vomiting of blood or bloody stools; if heartburn has lasted for 3 months or more; if dizziness, drowsiness or cold sweat occurs at the same time; if you have chest or shoulder pain with shortness of breath; if chest pain occurs often; if you have unexpected weight loss, nausea, vomiting or gastrointestinal pain; if you have had hypersensitivity to medicines; if you have kidney impairment, heart disease or liver impairment; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you are on haemodialysis.

If your body functions change after taking this medicine compared with before, consult a pharmacist. If symptoms do not improve, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not take this medicine for 14 days or more.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, a medicine for athlete's foot or an antifungal (itraconazole, posaconazole oral suspension and the like), or a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (dasatinib, erlotinib, gefitinib, pazopanib and the like). Consult a pharmacist if you are being given an intravenous lipid preparation. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: shock, anaphylaxis, difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, swelling of the face, swelling of the throat, urticaria; reduced white blood cells, red blood cells, platelets or eosinophils, anaemia, delayed clotting; Stevens-Johnson syndrome, epidermal necrolysis, rash, urticaria (erythema); abnormal liver function, raised AST (GOT) and ALT (GPT), raised total bilirubin and LDH, jaundice, hepatitis; muscle pain, rhabdomyolysis, joint pain, muscle cramps; slow heartbeat, rapid heartbeat, chest pain, raised blood pressure, facial flushing; ringing in the ears, disturbance of consciousness, convulsions, general lassitude, headache, drowsiness, insomnia, hallucination, agitation, excitement, reduced libido, abnormal sensation, a heavy head, confusion, depression, dizziness; constipation, diarrhoea, thirst, nausea and vomiting, abdominal distension, loss of appetite, stomatitis; interstitial nephritis, acute renal failure, fever, abnormal kidney function test values (raised BUN and creatinine and the like); menstrual disturbance; interstitial pneumonia with high fever, cough, difficulty breathing and abnormal chest X-ray; bronchospasm; breast enlargement in men; or taste disturbance.

groups.title: Tablet (246501ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment of liver disease caused by insufficient bile secretion and of diseases of the biliary system (bile duct, gallbladder), for the improvement of liver function in chronic liver disease, and for indigestion caused by the after-effects of small bowel resection and by inflammatory small bowel disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 0.5 to 1 tablet (50 to 100 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; severe obstruction of the bile duct; fulminant hepatitis; radio-opaque calcified gallstones; a non-functioning gallbladder; acute cholecystitis; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child; if you have kidney disease; if you have peptic ulcer (acute gastric or duodenal ulcer); if you have large or small bowel inflammation such as Crohn's disease; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe pancreatic disease, gallstones, variceal bleeding, hepatic coma or ascites, or if you need a liver transplant.

Do not take it together with an oral diabetes medicine (tolbutamide), cholestyramine, colestipol, medicinal charcoal, antacids containing magnesium or aluminium hydroxide, medicines that increase cholesterol secretion from the liver (oral contraceptives containing oestrogen, lipid-lowering medicines such as clofibrate) or medicines that damage the liver.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: occasionally diarrhoea, nausea or vomiting; rarely abdominal pain, constipation, heartburn or stomach discomfort; occasionally itching; rarely rash, fever, cough, difficulty breathing or interstitial pneumonia with abnormal chest X-ray; rarely general lassitude, dizziness, calcification of gallstones, raised liver enzyme values (ALT, ALP, AST, gamma-GT) or reduced white blood cells.

groups.title: Oral Suspension (227730ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to remove bubbles in the bowel during gastroscopy, to remove gas in the bowel during abdominal X-ray examination, and to improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract (a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, aerophagia and the like).
groups.usage: Adults: to remove bubbles in the bowel for gastroscopy, take 40 to 80 mg with about 10 mL of water 15 to 40 minutes before the examination. To remove gas in the bowel for abdominal X-ray examination, take 40 to 80 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or between meals, starting 3 to 4 days before the examination. To improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract, take 40 to 80 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or at bedtime. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have asthma.

Shake it well before use.

Occasionally loose stools, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, nausea, a feeling of heaviness in the abdomen or loss of appetite, and rarely headache or mild irritation of the skin, eyes or mucous membranes may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (566833ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of selenium in people with selenium deficiency that cannot be made up by nutritional intake.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet (100 micrograms as selenium), 1 time in 1 day; the dose may be increased to a maximum of 2 tablets (200 micrograms as selenium) in 1 day. Take this medicine with water, without chewing it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have selenium toxicity; or if you have hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase deficiency.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with a reducing agent such as vitamin C. If you want to take vitamin C, take it separately with an interval of about 4 hours from this medicine. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, vomiting or allergy occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (254000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Drowsiness may occur while taking it; avoid driving a car or operating machinery. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine. Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor used for depression or Parkinson's disease, or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Consult a pharmacist if you are being given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, a cerebrovascular event such as stroke, abnormal sensation, myocardial infarction or ischaemic colitis occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs with urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, or if Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, general lassitude, liver function disorder with jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.
